# Initial Setup: Running Tests in Rancher

> Source: [Team White SharePoint](https://ascensus0.sharepoint.com/sites/TeamWhiteCF/SitePages/MTP-Initial-Setup-Running-Tests-in-Rancher-315557114.aspx) | Created: 2025-04-01 | Last modified: 2025-04-08 | Author: Chris Reynolds | Last editor: Diego Emanuel Travieso

---

To kick off the tests from your development PC you'll need some further setup.  These instructions were mostly transcribed from the following video tutorial: [Performance Testing Walkthrough](https://ascensus0.sharepoint.com/sites/PerformanceTestingTutorials/_layouts/15/stream.aspx?id=/sites/PerformanceTestingTutorials/Shared%20Documents/Performance%20Testing%20Tutorials/3.%20Performance%20-%20Walkthrough.mp4&ga=1&referrer=StreamWebApp.Web&referrerScenario=AddressBarCopied.view.5821b177-b80d-4a7c-bd1a-b5c8de4649b6)

#### Install Helm

1. Go to helm github: [https://github.com/helm/helm](https://github.com/helm/helm)
2. Download the latest release
3. Extract files into a known location which will be used for kubernetes (for example: "C:\Tools\kubernetes", which would directly contain helm.exe)
4. Add the installation path to environment variables
5.
  1. You should now be able to validate installation by executing the following command:   > helm version

#### Install Kubernetes

1. Enter the following URL into the browser to begin the download:   [https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.25.0/bin/windows/amd64/kubectl.exe](https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.25.0/bin/windows/amd64/kubectl.exe)
2. Copy kubectl.exe into the folder created in step 1C above
3.
  1. You should now be able to validate installation by executing the following command:   > kubectl version --short

#### Setup KUBECONFIG

1. Navigate to [rancher.ascensus.com](http://rancher.ascensus.com)
2. Under the Global items at the top-right of the page, click into k8s-env-test, which should bring you here:   [https://rancher.ascensus.com/c/c-gcjtt/monitoring](https://rancher.ascensus.com/c/c-gcjtt/monitoring)
3. Click the button for Kubeconfig File in the upper-right
4. Use the button at the bottom of the view to copy the contents to clipboard
5. Create a new file named "kube.yml" in the same path used in step 1C above and paste in the contents from step 3D
6. Open Environment Variables and create a new variable named KUBECONFIG.  Set the value to the full-path of the "kube.yml" file, like "C:\Tools\kubernetes\kube.yml"
7.
  1. You should now be able to validate setup by executing the following command:   > kubectl describe nodes

**Note:** When setting up kubernetes according to the previous guide, Rancher Desktop will not be able to run properly on the local machine. One way to allow Rancher Destop to run properly is to rename the KUBECONFIG environment variable, so local Rancher does not use the configuration described above and runs with the local configurations.

A better way is to add the rancher-desktop configs to the kube.yml. Add values as described in each section of the kube.yml file so there is a rancher-desktop cluster, a rancher-desktop user and a rancher-desktop context. When Rancher runs for the first time it will replace the values with real ones.

clusters:   - name: rancher-desktop     cluster:       server: https://127.0.0.1:6443       certificate-authority-data: #some generated content here       insecure-skip-tls-verify: false users:   - name: rancher-desktop     user:       client-certificate-data: #some generated content here       client-key-data: #some generated content here contexts:   - name: rancher-desktop     context:       cluster: rancher-desktop       name: rancher-desktop       user: rancher-desktop

The full file should look something like this:

apiVersion: v1 kind: Config clusters:   - name: k8s-env-test     cluster:       server: https://rancher.ascensus.com/k8s/clusters/c-gcjtt       certificate-authority-data:        insecure-skip-tls-verify: false   - name: k8s-env-test-rdre1-dkubtml01     cluster:       server: https://10.120.122.208:6443       certificate-authority-data:        insecure-skip-tls-verify: false   - name: rancher-desktop     cluster:       server: https://127.0.0.1:6443       certificate-authority-data:        insecure-skip-tls-verify: false users:   - name: k8s-env-test     user:       token: [REDACTED]   - name: rancher-desktop     user:       client-certificate-data:        client-key-data:  contexts:   - name: k8s-env-test     context:       cluster: k8s-env-test       name: k8s-env-test       user: k8s-env-test   - name: k8s-env-test-rdre1-dkubtml01     context:       cluster: k8s-env-test-rdre1-dkubtml01       name: k8s-env-test-rdre1-dkubtml01       user: k8s-env-test   - name: rancher-desktop     context:       cluster: rancher-desktop       name: rancher-desktop       user: rancher-desktop preferences: {} current-context: k8s-env-test

Now depending on the need, the current-context entry can be switched between k8s-env-test to run the performance tests and rancher-desktop to run Rancher Desktop locally and be able to dock instances such as RabbitMQ.
